root_cause: Access port assigned to wrong VLAN (Fa0/3 is in VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 10)
evidence: SW1# show vlan brief | VLAN10 ACCTG active Fa0/2 | VLAN20 SALES active Fa0/3
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: Access port assigned to wrong VLAN (Fa0/3 is in VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 10). Re-run 'show vlan brief' to verify.

root_cause: VLAN 30 not included in the trunk's allowed VLAN list
evidence: SW1# show interfaces trunk | Port Gi0/1 Vlans allowed: 1,10,20 | Vlans allowed and active: 1,10,20
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: VLAN 30 not included in the trunk's allowed VLAN list. Re-run 'show vlan brief' to verify.

root_cause: Trunk not carrying VLAN 30 between SW1 and SW2 (allowed-VLAN list issue)
evidence: show interfaces trunk output on both switches
fix_steps: Add VLAN 30 to the trunk's allowed list on both switches.

root_cause: VLAN 40 was never created on the switch (vlan database missing entry)
evidence: SW1# show vlan brief | (VLAN 40 not listed) || SW1# show run | interface vlan40 -> % Invalid input
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: VLAN 40 was never created on the switch (vlan database missing entry). Re-run 'show vlan brief' to verify.

root_cause: PC1 configured with wrong default gateway (192.168.1.100 instead of .1)
evidence: PC1> ipconfig | Gateway: 192.168.1.100 || R1# show ip interface brief | Gi0/0 192.168.1.1 up up
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: PC1 configured with wrong default gateway (192.168.1.100 instead of .1). Re-run 'show ip interface brief' to verify.

root_cause: Router sub-interface for VLAN 20 is administratively shut down
evidence: R1# show ip interface brief | Gi0/0.20 192.168.20.1 administratively down down
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: Router sub-interface for VLAN 20 is administratively shut down. Re-run 'show ip interface brief' to verify.

root_cause: DHCP server assigned an incorrect gateway option to PC3
evidence: PC3 ipconfig output
fix_steps: Check the DHCP pool's default-router statement.

root_cause: Duplicate IP address: PC5 was statically configured with the router's gateway address
evidence: PC1> arp -a | 192.168.1.1 aaaa.bbbb.0001 || PC5> ipconfig | IP: 192.168.1.1 (statically set)
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: Duplicate IP address: PC5 was statically configured with the router's gateway address. Re-run 'show ip interface brief' to verify.

root_cause: DHCP pool for VLAN 10 is exhausted (no addresses available)
evidence: R1# show ip dhcp pool VLAN10 | Total addresses: 30 | Leased: 30 | Available: 0
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: DHCP pool for VLAN 10 is exhausted (no addresses available). Re-run 'show ip dhcp pool' to verify.

root_cause: Missing 'ip helper-address' on the VLAN 20 sub-interface to relay DHCP broadcasts
evidence: R1# show run interface Gi0/0.20 | ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0 (no ip helper-address line present)
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: Missing 'ip helper-address' on the VLAN 20 sub-interface to relay DHCP broadcasts. Re-run 'show ip dhcp pool' to verify.

root_cause: DHCP pool VLAN30 is configured with the wrong network statement
evidence: R1# show run | ip dhcp pool VLAN30 -> network 192.168.99.0 255.255.255.0
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: DHCP pool VLAN30 is configured with the wrong network statement. Re-run 'show ip dhcp pool' to verify.

root_cause: DHCP pool for VLAN 10 is exhausted (no addresses available)
evidence: show ip dhcp pool VLAN10 output
fix_steps: Increase the DHCP pool size or reduce lease time.

root_cause: DHCP option 6 (DNS server) is pointing at the wrong host IP
evidence: PC2> ipconfig /all | DNS Servers: 192.168.1.250 (should be .200, the real DNS host)
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: DHCP option 6 (DNS server) is pointing at the wrong host IP. Re-run 'show access-lists' to verify.

root_cause: ACL 101 blocks UDP/53 (DNS) traffic before any permit statement is reached
evidence: R1# show access-lists 101 | deny udp any any eq 53 (before any DNS permit line)
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: ACL 101 blocks UDP/53 (DNS) traffic before any permit statement is reached. Re-run 'show access-lists' to verify.

root_cause: Missing 'ip name-server <dns-ip>' statement on the router
evidence: R1# show run | ip domain-lookup | (no 'ip name-server' line present)
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: Missing 'ip name-server <dns-ip>' statement on the router. Re-run 'show access-lists' to verify.

root_cause: PC4 has a stale statically-configured DNS entry left over from a previous network
evidence: PC4> ipconfig /all | DNS Servers: 10.10.10.10 (stale entry, statically set, not matching current network's DHCP-issued DNS)
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: PC4 has a stale statically-configured DNS entry left over from a previous network. Re-run 'show access-lists' to verify.

root_cause: Missing static route on R1 for the 172.16.0.0/24 network via R2
evidence: R1# show ip route | 172.16.0.0 -- (no matching route line present)
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: Missing static route on R1 for the 172.16.0.0/24 network via R2. Re-run 'show ip route' to verify.

root_cause: R2 is not advertising its LAN network (192.168.20.0) into RIP
evidence: R2# show run | router rip | version 2 | network 10.0.0.0 (192.168.20.0 network statement missing)
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: R2 is not advertising its LAN network (192.168.20.0) into RIP. Re-run 'show ip route' to verify.

root_cause: OSPF area number mismatch between R1 (area 0) and R2 (area 1) on the shared link
evidence: R1# show ip ospf interface Gi0/1 | Area 0 || R2# show ip ospf interface Gi0/1 | Area 1
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: OSPF area number mismatch between R1 (area 0) and R2 (area 1) on the shared link. Re-run 'show ip route' to verify.

root_cause: Missing static route on R1 for the 172.16.20.0/24 network
evidence: show ip route 172.16.20.0 output
fix_steps: Add a static route for 172.16.20.0/24.

root_cause: ACL 110 has no permit statement for the 192.168.10.0/24 subnet, so all traffic is denied
evidence: R1# show access-lists 110 | 10 deny ip any any | (implicit/explicit deny-all is the only line, no permit statements)
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: ACL 110 has no permit statement for the 192.168.10.0/24 subnet, so all traffic is denied. Re-run 'show access-lists' to verify.

root_cause: ACL 120 applied in the wrong direction (in instead of out) on the sub-interface
evidence: R1# show run interface Gi0/0.40 | ip access-group 120 in (intended direction was out)
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: ACL 120 applied in the wrong direction (in instead of out) on the sub-interface. Re-run 'show access-lists' to verify.

root_cause: ACL statement order denies the entire 192.168.10.0/24 subnet (line 20) instead of only the intended host
evidence: R1# show access-lists 130 | 10 deny ip host 192.168.10.15 any | 20 deny ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 any | 30 permit ip any any
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: ACL statement order denies the entire 192.168.10.0/24 subnet (line 20) instead of only the intended host. Re-run 'show access-lists' to verify.

root_cause: NAT overload not translating return traffic from the web server
evidence: show ip nat translations output
fix_steps: Verify NAT inside/outside interface markings.

root_cause: NAT overload command exists, but the inside/outside interfaces were never marked, so no translation occurs
evidence: R1# show ip nat translations | (empty) || R1# show run | (no 'ip nat inside'/'ip nat outside' interface commands found)
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: NAT overload command exists, but the inside/outside interfaces were never marked, so no translation occurs. Re-run 'show ip nat translations' to verify.

root_cause: NAT's referenced ACL only permits 192.168.10.0/24, leaving 192.168.20.0/24 untranslated
evidence: R1# show access-lists 1 | 10 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 | (192.168.20.0 network not included)
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: NAT's referenced ACL only permits 192.168.10.0/24, leaving 192.168.20.0/24 untranslated. Re-run 'show ip nat translations' to verify.

root_cause: Interfaces were never explicitly marked with 'ip nat inside' / 'ip nat outside'
evidence: R1# show ip nat statistics | Inside interfaces: (none) | Outside interfaces: (none)
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: Interfaces were never explicitly marked with 'ip nat inside' / 'ip nat outside'. Re-run 'show ip nat translations' to verify.

root_cause: Static NAT mapping references the wrong internal port (8080) instead of the server's actual port (80)
evidence: R1# show run | ip nat inside source static tcp 192.168.10.100 8080 203.0.113.10 80 (internal port mismatch: server actually listens on 80, not 8080)
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: Static NAT mapping references the wrong internal port (8080) instead of the server's actual port (80). Re-run 'show ip nat translations' to verify.

root_cause: Passphrase mismatch between the client (lowercase, missing symbol) and the AP's configured key
evidence: AP# show running-config | ssid CORP-WIFI | authentication key: Cisco123! || Laptop entered passphrase: cisco123
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: Passphrase mismatch between the client (lowercase, missing symbol) and the AP's configured key. Re-run 'show interface dot11radio0' to verify.

root_cause: Wireless channel overlap causing dropped guest sessions
evidence: AP radio configuration
fix_steps: Change one AP to a non-overlapping channel.

root_cause: Co-channel interference: both APs are set to the same 2.4GHz channel (6) in overlapping coverage areas
evidence: AP1# show interface dot11radio0 | Channel: 6 || AP2# show interface dot11radio0 | Channel: 6
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: Co-channel interference: both APs are set to the same 2.4GHz channel (6) in overlapping coverage areas. Re-run 'show interface dot11radio0' to verify.

root_cause: AP's uplink switch port is set to access mode VLAN 1 instead of trunking VLAN 60 to the DHCP relay router
evidence: SW1# show interfaces Fa0/5 switchport | Administrative Mode: static access | Access Mode VLAN: 1
fix_steps: Correct the configuration so it matches: AP's uplink switch port is set to access mode VLAN 1 instead of trunking VLAN 60 to the DHCP relay router. Re-run 'show interface dot11radio0' to verify.
